source_body_en: Abstract Monitoring the locomotor activity of mosquitoes is vital for understanding their behavioral patterns and role in disease transmission. Studies investigating the locomotor activity of dengue-infected mosquitoes have faced several limitations, including confining mosquitoes within small tubes that restrict natural movement, discontinuous recordings that fail to provide detailed activity patterns, and the lack of open-source tools to effectively monitor mosquito locomotor activity. Here, we present LocoTrackAI, a robust artificial intelligence-based tool that leverages a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a multi-object tracking algorithm to comprehensively analyze the locomotor activity of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes from videos recorded using standard laboratory cages. LocoTrackAI automatically processes video datasets, tracks individual mosquito identities, and provides detailed locomotion results for both individual mosquitoes and group activity, including spatial distributions, movement patterns, heat maps, and activity ratios. The tool features a Skip Frame function to improve computational efficiency, adjustable movement thresholds for customized sensitivity, and a user-friendly interface that supports unsupervised batch processing, ensuring accuracy and flexibility for diverse research applications. The LocoTrackAI achieved 99.91% accuracy with a low centroid detection error of 0.22 pixels across 36,020 frames and demonstrated a 93.23% success rate in reassigning identities during 207 post-occlusion instances. Using LocoTrackAI, we analyzed the locomotor activity of dengue-infected and noninfected mosquitoes across 3.24 million recorded mosquito positions. Results revealed that infected mosquitoes exhibited significantly higher locomotor activity (p = 0.0009), with 95,726 movements (0.30 mean locomotor activity) compared to 42,173 movements (0.13 mean locomotor activity) in noninfected mosquitoes, representing more than 200% of the activity of noninfected mosquitoes. Additionally, spatial analysis indicated a more extensive and uniform distribution for infected mosquitoes, with entropy values of 3.38 for infected and 3.13 for noninfected mosquitoes. These findings suggest that dengue infection increases locomotor activity and spatial exploration, potentially enhancing the mosquitoes' capacity to locate hosts and spread the virus. Future studies could expand on this work by investigating the locomotor effects of other arboviruses and further developing tools to automate the analysis of feeding and other critical behaviors.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 监测蚊子的运动活动对于了解其行为模式和在疾病 传播 中的作用至关重要。调查感染登革热的蚊子的运动活动的研究面临着一些限制,包括将蚊子限制在限制自然运动的小管内、无法提供详细活动模式的不连续记录以及缺乏有效监测蚊子运动活动的开源工具。
analysis_zh.methods: LocoTrackAI 自动处理视频数据集,跟踪个体蚊子身份,并提供个体蚊子和群体活动的详细运动结果,包括空间分布、运动模式、热图和活动比率。该工具具有跳帧功能,可提高计算效率,可调节移动阈值以定制灵敏度,以及支持无监督批处理的用户友好界面,确保各种研究应用的准确性和灵活性。
analysis_zh.main_results: LocoTrackAI 在 36,020 帧中实现了 99.91% 的准确率,质心检测误差低至 0.22 像素,并在 207 个遮挡后实例中重新分配身份的成功率达到 93.23%。结果显示,受感染的蚊子表现出显着更高的运动活动(p = 0.0009),与未受感染的蚊子的 42,173 次运动(平均运动活动为 0.30)相比,有 95,726 次运动(平均运动活动为 0.13),相当于未受感染的蚊子活动的 200% 以上。此外,空间分析表明受感染蚊子的分布更加广泛和均匀,受感染蚊子的熵值为 3.38,未受感染蚊子的熵值为 3.13。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,登革热感染增加了运动活动和空间探索,可能增强蚊子定位 宿主 和传播病毒的能力。未来的研究可以通过调查其他虫媒病毒的运动效应并进一步开发自动分析进食和其他关键行为的工具来扩展这项工作。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: LocoTrackAI的开发为监测蚊子行为提供了强大的工具,可以增强对登革热传播动态的了解并为媒介控制策略提供信息。感染登革热的蚊子运动活动的增加凸显了有针对性的干预措施减少蚊子-宿主 接触和疾病传播的潜力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在实验室环境中使用标准笼子进行的,这可能无法完全复制自然环境条件。尽管准确性和统计显着性很高,但由于报告仅具有摘要性质并且需要在现场环境中进一步验证,因此证据强度适中。

title: A dengue sob uma perspectiva epidemiológica e sociodemográfica: uma análise sobre o estado de Minas Gerais
abstract: O contexto epidemiológico da dengue no Brasil caracteriza-se por oscilações entre períodos endêmicos e surtos epidêmicos, representando um desafio contínuo à saúde pública. Este estudo tem como objetivo geral analisar o perfil epidemiológico e sociodemográfico da dengue no estado de Minas Gerais, com ênfase no município de Uberlândia, a partir de evidências da literatura científica recente. Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de caráter descritivo e exploratório, realizada em bases de dados nacionais e internacionais. Os resultados indicam elevada incidência da doença em determinados períodos do ano, forte associação com fatores socioambientais, desigualdades regionais e impacto significativo sobre o Sistema Único de Saúde. Conclui-se que a dengue permanece como um importante problema de saúde pública em Minas Gerais, exigindo estratégias integradas de vigilância epidemiológica, controle vetorial e ações intersetoriais.

Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de caráter descritivo e exploratório, realizada em bases de dados nacionais e internacionais. Os resultados indicam elevada incidência da doença em determinados períodos do ano, forte associação com fatores socioambientais, desigualdades regionais e impacto significativo sobre o Sistema Único de Saúde. Conclui-se que a dengue permanece como um importante problema de saúde pública em Minas Gerais, exigindo estratégias integradas de vigilância epidemiológica, controle vetorial e ações intersetoriais.

title: De veranderende epidemiologie van vectorziekten
abstract: Het augustusnummer van het Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde en Gezondheidszorg bevat een bijdrage over virusinfecties met “exotische” muggen in de rol van vector (1). Intuïtief maken wij dan de associatie met verre reizen. Maar, er is meer aan de hand. “Vector-borne diseases” of vectorziekten vertegenwoordigen 17% van alle infectieziekten wereldwijd en zijn verantwoordelijk voor meer dan 700.000 overlijdens per jaar (2, 3). Die vectoren zijn artropoden (zoals muggen en teken) die pathogene micro-organismen (virussen, parasieten of bacteriën) kunnen overdragen op een gastheer wanneer zij een bloedmaaltijd gebruiken (2). Het gaat over koortsige ziekten zoals bijvoorbeeld malaria, gele koorts, dengue, chikungunya en zika. Het risico om zo een infectie op te lopen, is het grootst in die delen van de wereld met een warm en vochtig klimaat (3). Maar, in de voorbije 2 decennia was er een merkelijke toename in incidentie en verdeling van sommige van deze ziekten in Europa (4, 5). Dat heeft deels te maken met de toenemende globalisering, meer intercontinentaal reisverkeer en handelstranport wereldwijd, wat de verspreiding van vectoren in de hand werkt (4, 6). Terugkerende reizigers kunnen inderdaad een door vectoren overgebrachte infectie oplopen als “importziekte” omdat zij tijdens hun verblijf in een endemische streek gestoken werden door exotische muggen. Maar toch wordt ook in Europa in toenemende mate “autochtone transmissie” van door muggen overdraagbare pathogenen beschreven (7). De transmissie gebeurt dan doordat een teruggekeerde reiziger met viremie in eigen land geprikt wordt door een mug die een geschikte vector is, daarbij het pathogene micro-organisme opneemt en het dan doorgeeft aan een nog niet geïnfecteerd iemand bij een volgende prik (6). Een essentiële voorwaarde voor dit mechanisme is uiteraard dat de vector zich in het nieuwe land gevestigd heeft en zich daar kan handhaven. Meer en meer wordt aangenomen dat de klimaatverandering in belangrijke mate dit process aandrijft (8, 9). Hogere temperaturen, andere neerslagpatronen en zachtere winters zouden de vestiging en verspreiding van vectorartropoden in voordien niet-endemische regio’s mogelijk maken. Het gaat dan vooral om muggen van het species Aedes, Anopheles en Culex, en “sandflies” van het species Phlebotomus (8). Het ectothermische karakter van deze artropoden, die de eigen lichaamstemperatuur niet kunnen reguleren, maakt hen zeer gevoelig aan externe klimaatomstandigheden. Daarnaast is de omgevingstemperatuur mee bepalend voor de maturatie en replicatie van de pathogenen die door die atropoden meegedragen worden (10, 11). Op dezelfde manier wordt overigens ook de natuurlijke epidemiologie beïnvloed van ziekten die reeds autochtoon waren in Europa, zoals leishmaniasis, met sandflies als vector, en infectie met West Nile-virus, met Culex-muggen als vector (8). Aedes albopictus of de Aziatische tijgermug, vector van arbovirussen zoals dengue en chikungunya, is een voorbeeld bij uitstek van een exotische muggensoort die zich gestaag blijft verspreiden over het Europese continent na daar voor het eerst verschenen te zijn in de late jaren 70. Zo werd de eerste autochtone uitbraak van chikungunya in Europa gedocumenteerd in Italië in 2007, en van dengue in Kroatië in 2010. Later volgden herhaalde uitbraken van deze ziekten in Italië, Frankrijk en Spanje (6, 12). België ligt op het pad van de verder noordwaartse verplaatsing van deze mug, die zich er in toenemende mate vestigt en ook overwintert. Dat is gebleken uit projecten van surveillance, zoals MEMO en MEMO+ (acroniem voor “Monitoring of Exotic Mosquitoes”) als onderdeel van het groter “National Environmental Health Action Plan” of NEHAP (13, 14, 15). Observaties in andere delen van de wereld hebben aangetoond dat plaatselijke uitbraken van virusziekte overgebracht door Aedes-muggen zich typisch voordeden met een interval van 5 tot 15 jaar nadat deze muggensoort zich gevestigd had (5, 16). Europese data lijken de mogelijkheid van een dergelijk patroon te ondersteunen, want zij tonen een sterke toename van autochtone gevallen van dengue in landen waar Aedes albopictus al sinds meerdere jaren gedijt (5). Deze bevindingen moeten ons er dus toe aanzetten om de kans op een ernstige infectieziekte overgebracht door muggen niet meer louter als een “ver-van-mijn-bedhypothese” weg te dringen wanneer in de anamnese een typische hint zoals “terugkeer van een verre reis” ontbreekt. Want hoewel nu misschien nog geen vaste prik in onze standaardlijst van differentiaaldiagnosen van een koortsige ziekte, kan de optie van een door muggen overdraagbare infectie in de toekomst mogelijk vaker het overwegen waard worden. Patrick Lacor, hoofdredacteur

Op dezelfde manier wordt overigens ook de natuurlijke epidemiologie beïnvloed van ziekten die reeds autochtoon waren in Europa, zoals leishmaniasis, met sandflies als vector, en infectie met West Nile-virus, met Culex-muggen als vector (8). Aedes albopictus of de Aziatische tijgermug, vector van arbovirussen zoals dengue en chikungunya, is een voorbeeld bij uitstek van een exotische muggensoort die zich gestaag blijft verspreiden over het Europese continent na daar voor het eerst verschenen te zijn in de late jaren 70. Zo werd de eerste autochtone uitbraak van chikungunya in Europa gedocumenteerd in Italië in 2007, en van dengue in Kroatië in 2010. Later volgden herhaalde uitbraken van deze ziekten in Italië, Frankrijk en Spanje (6, 12). België ligt op het pad van de verder noordwaartse verplaatsing van deze mug, die zich er in toenemende mate vestigt en ook overwintert. Dat is gebleken uit projecten van surveillance, zoals MEMO en MEMO+ (acroniem voor “Monitoring of Exotic Mosquitoes”) als onderdeel van het groter “National Environmental Health Action Plan” of NEHAP (13, 14, 15). Observaties in andere delen van de wereld hebben aangetoond dat plaatselijke uitbraken van virusziekte overgebracht door Aedes-muggen zich typisch voordeden met een interval van 5 tot 15 jaar nadat deze muggensoort zich gevestigd had (5, 16). Europese data lijken de mogelijkheid van een dergelijk patroon te ondersteunen, want zij tonen een sterke toename van autochtone gevallen van dengue in landen waar Aedes albopictus al sinds meerdere jaren gedijt (5). Deze bevindingen moeten ons er dus toe aanzetten om de kans op een ernstige infectieziekte overgebracht door muggen niet meer louter als een “ver-van-mijn-bedhypothese” weg te dringen wanneer in de anamnese een typische hint zoals “terugkeer van een verre reis” ontbreekt. Want hoewel nu misschien nog geen vaste prik in onze standaardlijst van differentiaaldiagnosen van een koortsige ziekte, kan de optie van een door muggen overdraagbare infectie in de toekomst mogelijk vaker het overwegen waard worden. analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a narrative review article published in the Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde en Gezondheidszorg, discussing global and European epidemiological trends of vector-borne diseases without primary data collection.
analysis.methods: The review synthesizes existing literature and surveillance data on vector-borne diseases, including projects like MEMO and MEMO+, to analyze the spread of exotic mosquitoes and autochthonous transmission patterns in Europe.
analysis.main_results: Vector-borne diseases represent 17% of all infectious diseases globally, causing over 700,000 deaths annually; Europe has seen a marked increase in incidence and distribution of diseases like dengue and chikungunya, with autochthonous transmission documented in Italy, Croatia, France, and Spain.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the changing epidemiology of vector-borne diseases, particularly the emergence of exotic mosquito-borne infections in Europe. It highlights that vector-borne diseases constitute 17% of global infectious diseases, causing over 700,000 deaths annually. The study attributes the rise in autochthonous transmission of diseases like dengue and chikungunya in Europe to climate change, globalization, and the establishment of exotic vectors such as Aedes albopictus. Surveillance projects like MEMO and MEMO+ document the northward spread of these vectors, with outbreaks occurring 5-15 years after their introduction. The authors emphasize the need to reconsider differential diagnoses for febrile illnesses, as locally transmitted mosquito-borne infections may become more common in previously non-endemic regions.

title: Sequence Homology and Tissue Tropism Determine Superinfection Exclusion of Zika virus in Aedes aegypti Mediated by an insect-specific Binjari-Zika Virus Chimera
abstract: Arboviruses such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses cause widespread disease and continue to expand their geographical range due to climate change and vector spread. Insect-specific flaviviruses (ISFs) are promising biocontrol candidates of arboviruses, due to recent studies showing that prior infection with an ISF can reduce arbovirus replication in mosquitoes through superinfection exclusion (SIE). However, the route of infection, tissue tropism, pathogenesis and the mechanisms underlying SIE of ISFs in mosquitoes remain unclear. RNA interference (RNAi) is a potent antiviral response in insects, therefore it is expected that sequence homology between the ISF and the arbovirus will strengthen SIE. Here, we used ISF Binjari virus and a chimera containing the Zika virus structural proteins prME (BinJ-ZIKV) as a model system. Intrathoracic injection of BinJ-ZIKV in Aedes aegypti led to rapid systemic infection that excluded the midgut, subsequently blocking ZIKV dissemination from the midgut. SIE was strongest in tissues where primary-virus replication was highest. This spatial component of SIE was stronger when there was sequence homology between the ISF and arbovirus and displayed a strong 21nt siRNA response, suggesting RNAi contributed to the observed SIE. Upon oral inoculation, BinJ-ZIKV replicated efficiently in mosquitoes, was detected across multiple tissues, and saliva. BinJ-ZIKV also had higher infection establishment than BinJV at lower oral titres. SIE was observed for BinJ-ZIKV infection after oral exposure interfered with subsequent ZIKV midgut infection. Together, these findings support engineered ISF-chimeras as valuable experimental tools to dissect viral determinants of SIE and to optimize mosquito-based arbovirus interference strategies.

The research was conducted through intrathoracic injection and oral inoculation of BinJ-ZIKV to observe its effects on subsequent ZIKV infection.

SIE was strongest in tissues where primary-virus replication was highest, and the spatial component of SIE was stronger when there was sequence homology between the ISF and arbovirus.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the mechanisms of superinfection exclusion (SIE) in mosquitoes, particularly focusing on how sequence homology and tissue tropism influence SIE of arboviruses. Dengue viruses, which cause widespread disease, are of significant public health concern due to their expanding geographical range.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study used a model system involving the insect-specific Binjari virus and a Binjari-Zika virus chimera (BinJ-ZIKV) in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. The research was conducted through intrathoracic injection and oral inoculation of BinJ-ZIKV to observe its effects on subsequent ZIKV infection.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers employed RNA interference (RNAi) as a mechanism to analyze the antiviral response in mosquitoes. They injected BinJ-ZIKV intrathoracically and orally inoculated it to assess its impact on ZIKV dissemination and replication.
analysis_en.main_results: Intrathoracic injection of BinJ-ZIKV led to rapid systemic infection that excluded the midgut, thereby blocking ZIKV dissemination. SIE was strongest in tissues where primary-virus replication was highest, and the spatial component of SIE was stronger when there was sequence homology between the ISF and arbovirus.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that sequence homology and tissue tropism are critical factors in determining SIE, with RNAi playing a significant role. This study provides novel insights into the mechanisms of SIE and highlights the potential of engineered ISF-chimeras for understanding viral determinants of SIE.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results have implications for developing mosquito-based strategies to interfere with arbovirus transmission, potentially leading to improved biocontrol methods against dengue and other related viruses.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an abstract-only analysis, which may not capture detailed experimental procedures or outcomes. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on general observations and does not include specific numerical data or statistical analyses.

title_zh: 序列同源性和组织向性决定了昆虫特异性 Binjari-Zika 病毒嵌合体介导的埃及伊蚊中寨卡病毒的重复感染排除
source_body_en: Arboviruses such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses cause widespread disease and continue to expand their geographical range due to climate change and vector spread. Insect-specific flaviviruses (ISFs) are promising biocontrol candidates of arboviruses, due to recent studies showing that prior infection with an ISF can reduce arbovirus replication in mosquitoes through superinfection exclusion (SIE). However, the route of infection, tissue tropism, pathogenesis and the mechanisms underlying SIE of ISFs in mosquitoes remain unclear. RNA interference (RNAi) is a potent antiviral response in insects, therefore it is expected that sequence homology between the ISF and the arbovirus will strengthen SIE. Here, we used ISF Binjari virus and a chimera containing the Zika virus structural proteins prME (BinJ-ZIKV) as a model system. Intrathoracic injection of BinJ-ZIKV in Aedes aegypti led to rapid systemic infection that excluded the midgut, subsequently blocking ZIKV dissemination from the midgut. SIE was strongest in tissues where primary-virus replication was highest. This spatial component of SIE was stronger when there was sequence homology between the ISF and arbovirus and displayed a strong 21nt siRNA response, suggesting RNAi contributed to the observed SIE. Upon oral inoculation, BinJ-ZIKV replicated efficiently in mosquitoes, was detected across multiple tissues, and saliva. BinJ-ZIKV also had higher infection establishment than BinJV at lower oral titres. SIE was observed for BinJ-ZIKV infection after oral exposure interfered with subsequent ZIKV midgut infection. Together, these findings support engineered ISF-chimeras as valuable experimental tools to dissect viral determinants of SIE and to optimize mosquito-based arbovirus interference strategies.
abstract_zh: 登革热、寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅病毒等虫媒病毒会引起广泛的疾病,并由于气候变化和 媒介 传播而继续扩大其地理范围。昆虫特异性黄病毒 (ISF) 是有希望的虫媒病毒生物防治候选者,因为最近的研究表明,先前感染 ISF 可以通过重复感染排除 (SIE) 减少蚊子中虫媒病毒的复制。然而,蚊子中 ISF 的感染途径、组织向性、发病机制 和 SIE 的机制仍不清楚。RNA 干扰 (RNAi) 是昆虫中一种有效的 抗病毒药物 反应,因此预计 ISF 和虫媒病毒之间的序列同源性将加强 SIE。在这里,我们使用 ISF Binjari 病毒和包含寨卡病毒结构蛋白 prME (BinJ-ZIKV) 的嵌合体作为模型系统。埃及伊蚊胸腔内注射 BinJ-ZIKV 导致快速全身感染,排除中肠,随后阻止 ZIKV 从中肠传播。SIE 在原发病毒复制最高的组织中最强。当 ISF 和虫媒病毒之间存在序列同源性时,SIE 的这种空间成分更强,并表现出强烈的 21nt siRNA 响应,表明 RNAi 对观察到的 SIE 做出了贡献。口服接种后,BinJ-ZIKV 在蚊子体内有效复制,并在多个组织和唾液中检测到。BinJ-ZIKV 在较低的口服滴度下也比 BinJV 具有更高的感染建立率。在口服暴露干扰随后的 ZIKV 中肠感染后,观察到 BinJ-ZIKV 感染的 SIE。总之,这些发现支持工程 ISF 嵌合体作为有价值的实验工具来剖析 SIE 的病毒决定因素并优化基于蚊子的虫媒病毒干扰策略。

title: Molecular analysis and computational modeling reveal temporally separable responses triggered by DENV-induced soluble factors in endothelial cells
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) represents a growing global health challenge with billions of people at risk. Severe Dengue (SD), a complication of DENV infection that involves generalized hemorrhage, is driven, at least in part, by endothelial dysfunction. Endothelial dysfunction refers to increased permeability due to inflammation, mechanical injury and/or modification of the genetic program of endothelial cells. Previous work showed that exposure of endothelial cells to conditioned media from DENV-infected cells (CMDV) increased permeability and cellular stiffness, repressed endothelial markers and induced mesenchymal genes. However, the generality, extent, mechanism and ultimate impact of these events in the onset of SD remain elusive. Here, we integrate analysis from in vitro treatment of endothelial cells with media containing UV-inactivated DENV with computational modeling to investigate the key features of CMDV-induced endothelial alterations and their potential impact on endothelial dysfunction. We found that CMDV increased SNA1 and CDH2 expression, while suppressing endothelial genes OCLN and CDH5 . Global transcriptomics analysis revealed that CMDV triggered a transient pro-inflammatory response, followed by induction of selected tissue repair genes and matrix remodeling. A non-directed asynchronous network model (NDAM-CMDV) identified IL6 and FN1 as central nodes of DENV-induced endothelial trans-differentiation, providing new molecular insights that predict the evolution of the disease and identify potential therapeutic targets.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue virus (DENV) poses a major global health burden with severe dengue (SD) driven by endothelial dysfunction, yet the mechanisms linking DENV-induced soluble factors to endothelial alterations and SD onset remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used in vitro treatment of endothelial cells with conditioned media from DENV-infected cells (CMDV) and integrated transcriptomics with computational modeling to investigate endothelial responses.
analysis.methods: Endothelial cells were exposed to CMDV, and global transcriptomic profiling was performed to assess gene expression changes, followed by construction of a non-directed asynchronous network model (NDAM-CMDV) to identify central regulatory nodes.
analysis.main_results: CMDV exposure increased SNA1 and CDH2 expression while suppressing endothelial genes OCLN and CDH5, and triggered a transient pro-inflammatory response followed by induction of tissue repair and matrix remodeling genes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that DENV-induced soluble factors drive endothelial trans-differentiation, with IL6 and FN1 identified as central nodes in a network model that predicts disease evolution and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study suggests that targeting IL6 and FN1 pathways may mitigate endothelial dysfunction in dengue, informing future therapeutic strategies and surveillance approaches for severe dengue.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro models and computational predictions, lacking in vivo validation or clinical correlation, warranting cautious interpretation and further experimental confirmation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how soluble factors from DENV-infected cells alter endothelial cell function, a process implicated in severe dengue pathogenesis. Using in vitro exposure of endothelial cells to conditioned media from DENV-infected cells (CMDV), the authors observed increased expression of mesenchymal markers (SNA1, CDH2) and suppression of endothelial markers (OCLN, CDH5), alongside a transient pro-inflammatory response followed by tissue repair and matrix remodeling gene induction. Computational modeling identified IL6 and FN1 as central regulatory nodes in DENV-induced endothelial trans-differentiation, proposing these as potential therapeutic targets. While the findings provide mechanistic insights into endothelial dysfunction during dengue infection, the study is limited to in vitro and computational analyses without in vivo validation, constraining the strength of evidence and generalizability.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为 DENV 诱导的可溶性因子驱动内皮转分化的证据,其中 IL6 和 FN1 被确定为预测疾病 进化 和潜在治疗靶点的网络模型中的中心节点。

abstract_zh: 登革病毒 (DENV) 代表着日益严重的全球健康挑战,数十亿人面临风险。重症登革热 (SD) 是 DENV 感染的一种并发症,涉及全身出血,至少部分是由内皮功能障碍引起的。内皮功能障碍是指由于炎症、机械损伤和/或内皮细胞遗传程序的改变而导致的通透性增加。先前的研究表明,将内皮细胞暴露于来自 DENV 感染细胞 (CMDV) 的条件培养基中会增加通透性和细胞硬度,抑制内皮标记并诱导间充质基因。然而,这些事件对 SD 发病的普遍性、程度、机制和最终影响仍然难以捉摸。在这里,我们将内皮细胞的体外 治疗 分析与含有 UV 灭活 DENV 的培养基与计算模型相结合,以研究 CMDV 诱导的内皮改变的关键特征及其对内皮功能障碍的潜在影响。我们发现CMDV增加了SNA1和CDH2的表达,同时抑制了内皮基因OCLN和CDH5。全球转录组学分析显示,CMDV 引发短暂的促炎症反应,随后诱导选定的组织修复基因和基质重塑。非定向异步网络模型 (NDAM-CMDV) 确定 IL6 和 FN1 是 DENV 诱导的内皮转分化的中心节点,为预测疾病的 进化 并确定潜在的治疗靶点提供了新的分子见解。

title: Virus-specific alterations in placental structure and transporter expression following maternal arbovirus infection.
abstract: We hypothesized that arboviruses impair the placental expression of key functional markers implicated in fetal brain development. Singleton placentae (n = 54) affected by chikungunya (CHIKV, n = 12), dengue (DENV, n = 8), zika (ZIKV, n = 15), or healthy controls (HC, n = 15) were analysed. Immunohistochemical quantification of key transporter systems, cell turnover markers, and signalling pathways related to extracellular matrix remodelling, vascular maintenance, and nutrient sensing was undertaken. Maternal age and BMI were lower in CHIKV/ZIKV, whereas birth weight was reduced in DENV pregnancies compared with HC. CHIKV/ZIKV exhibited reduced syncytiotrophoblast area, CHIKV/DENV showed reduced syncytial knot area, whereas DENV showed increased fetal blood vessel and reduced connective tissue areas. Histopathology detected predominantly mild vascular and stromal lesions across groups, with DENV placentae exhibiting moderate congestion in 100% of cases. Decreased expression of P-gp, BCRP, ABCA1 and SNAT2 were detected in all groups. CHIKV/ZIKV also exhibited decreased GLUT1, while ZIKV showed reduced SNAT1 expression. MCT8 expression was significantly elevated in CHIKV. Placental Ki-67 was increased in CHIKV/ZIKV, indicating altered trophoblast turnover. VEGFB expression was reduced and p-mTOR signalling was increased across all arbovirus-exposed placentae, while MMP9 expression was unchanged. Principal components analysis (PCA) distinguished infected from uninfected groups based on placental functional markers related to fetal brain development, but not on histomorphometry. Arboviral-infected placentae showed distinct structural remodelling and altered transporter expression, potentially increasing fetal brain vulnerability and long-term neurodevelopmental risks, even in the absence of neonatal symptoms. KEY POINTS: Virus-specific placental histomorphometric changes were detected, including altered syncytiotrophoblast/syncytial knot, connective tissue and fetal blood vessel areas. Arboviruses reduced the placental efflux transporters P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) and disrupted the expression of ABCA1, SNAT2, GLUT1 and SNAT4 nutrient transporters, while ZIKV additionally reduced SNAT1 expression. Placental functional adaptation to arboviral infection comprised changes in the expression of placental markers of proliferation (Ki-67), angiogenesis (VEGFB), and nutrient sensing (p-mTOR). Arbovirus-exposed placentae exhibited greater functional alterations rather than overt structural pathology, suggesting potential subclinical effects on fetal neurodevelopment, even in the absence of major neonatal abnormalities.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether maternal arbovirus infection, including dengue virus (DENV), alters placental structure and transporter expression relevant to fetal brain development. Singleton placentae from pregnancies affected by chikungunya (CHIKV), dengue (DENV), zika (ZIKV), or healthy controls were analysed using immunohistochemistry and histomorphometry. DENV-exposed placentae showed increased fetal blood vessel area and reduced connective tissue area, alongside decreased expression of placental transporters (P-gp, BCRP, ABCA1, SNAT2) across all groups. Birth weight was lower in DENV pregnancies compared with controls. The authors concluded that arbovirus-exposed placentae exhibit virus-specific structural and functional alterations, potentially increasing fetal brain vulnerability even in the absence of neonatal symptoms. These findings suggest possible subclinical impacts on fetal growth and neurodevelopment, highlighting the need for surveillance and further mechanistic studies.

abstract_zh: 我们假设虫媒病毒会损害与胎儿大脑发育有关的关键功能标记物的胎盘表达。对受基孔肯雅热(CHIKV,n = 12)、登革热(DENV,n = 8)、寨卡病毒(ZIKV,n = 15)或健康对照(HC,n = 15)感染的单胎胎盘(n = 54)进行了分析。对关键转运系统、细胞周转标记物以及与细胞外基质重塑、血管维护和营养传感相关的信号通路进行免疫组织化学定量。与 HC 相比,CHIKV/ZIKV 孕妇的母亲年龄和 BMI 较低,而 DENV 妊娠的出生体重较低。CHIKV/ZIKV 表现出合体滋养层面积减少,CHIKV/DENV 表现出合胞结面积减少,而 DENV 表现出胎儿血管增加和结缔组织面积减少。组织病理学检测到各组主要有轻度血管和间质病变,100% 的病例中 DENV 胎盘表现出中度充血。所有组中均检测到 P-gp、BCRP、ABCA1 和 SNAT2 表达下降。CHIKV/ZIKV 也表现出 GLUT1 表达减少,而 ZIKV 表现出 SNAT1 表达减少。MCT8 表达在 CHIKV 中显着升高。CHIKV/ZIKV 中胎盘 Ki-67 增加,表明滋养层周转发生改变。在所有暴露于虫媒病毒的胎盘中,VEGFB 表达减少,p-mTOR 信号传导增加,而 MMP9 表达没有变化。主成分分析(PCA)根据与胎儿大脑发育相关的胎盘功能标记物(而不是组织形态计量学)区分感染组和未感染组。虫媒病毒感染的胎盘表现出明显的结构重塑和转运蛋白表达的改变,即使没有新生儿症状,也可能增加胎儿大脑的脆弱性和长期神经发育风险。要点:检测到病毒特异性胎盘组织形态学变化,包括合体滋养层/合胞结、结缔组织和胎儿血管区域的改变。虫媒病毒减少胎盘流出转运蛋白 P-糖蛋白 (P-gp) 和乳腺癌抗性蛋白 (BCRP),并破坏 ABCA1、SNAT2、GLUT1 和 SNAT4 营养转运蛋白的表达,而 ZIKV 还降低 SNAT1 表达。胎盘对虫媒病毒感染的功能适应包括胎盘增殖标记物 (Ki-67)、血管生成 (VEGFB) 和营养感应 (p-mTOR) 表达的变化。虫媒病毒暴露的胎盘表现出更大的功能改变,而不是明显的结构病理学改变,这表明即使在没有重大新生儿异常的情况下,也可能对胎儿神经发育产生潜在的亚临床影响。

title: Equi-depth pooling for standardized and cost-effective Adaptive Immune Receptor Repertoire sequencing (AIRRseq)
abstract: Bulk B- and T-cell adaptive immune receptor (BCR/TCR) repertoire sequencing (AIRRseq) enables comprehensive analysis of adaptive immune diversity, but achieving balanced sequencing depth across heterogeneous clinical samples remains a major cost driver. Standard equimolar pooling prior to sequencing disproportionately allocates reads, leading to undersequencing of libraries with high sequence abundance and oversampling of those with few sequences. Here, a quantitative pooling strategy is described in which libraries are pooled based on estimated target-specific unique molecular identifier (UMI) counts rather than library molarity, ensuring a uniform number of supporting reads per target sequence UMI across samples. Libraries were prepared from human RNA using the NEBNext Immune Sequencing (IS) kit and quantified by qPCR during the second amplification (PCR2) step. Deeply sequenced samples from a dengue 1 human infection model (DHIM1) clinical study were used to model the log-linear relationship between PCR2 cycle threshold (Ct) values and detected sequence counts. This model was then applied to a second, independent batch of samples from a dengue 3 human infection model (DHIM3) clinical study to predict UMI abundance and guide equi-depth pooling prior to sequencing. Sequencing of these equi-depth pools demonstrated a near-uniform reads-per-sequence ratio across samples, confirming that this approach achieves balanced depth without oversampling and at reduced cost. Simulations across a range of between-sample UMI-count distributions reflecting real-world sample pools showed that equi-depth pooling is expected to reduce the total number of required sequencing reads by approximately 70% compared with equimolar pooling, with savings increasing as the spread of library sizes grows. Beyond cost efficiency, equi-depth pooling eliminates the complexity-dependent sampling bias inherent to equimolar pooling, ensuring uniform sequencing depth and comparable UMI recovery across small and large libraries. For new workflows or sample types, implementation requires either an existing calibration dataset or a pilot sequencing experiment to establish the relationship between PCR2 Ct values and relative UMI abundance. The equi-depth method thus provides a robust, scalable, and cost-efficient strategy for bulk AIRRseq studies where library sizes vary widely.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces an equi-depth pooling strategy for AIRRseq to address the cost challenge of achieving balanced sequencing depth across heterogeneous clinical samples. By pooling libraries based on estimated target-specific UMI counts rather than library molarity, the method ensures uniform reads per target sequence UMI across samples. Applied to dengue infection model samples, it demonstrated near-uniform reads-per-sequence ratios, reducing sequencing reads by approximately 70% compared to equimolar pooling. The approach eliminates sampling bias and provides a cost-efficient, scalable solution for bulk AIRRseq studies, though it requires calibration data for new workflows.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了在批量 B 和 T 细胞适应性免疫受体库测序 (AIRRseq) 中实现跨异质临床样本的平衡测序深度的挑战,这仍然是主要的成本驱动因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用来自登革热1人类感染模型(DHIM1)临床研究的深度测序样本来模拟PCR2循环阈值(Ct)值和检测到的序列计数之间的关系,并将该模型应用于来自登革热3人类感染模型(DHIM3)临床研究的独立批次样本。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 NEBNext 免疫测序 (IS) 试剂盒从人类 RNA 中制备文库,并在第二个扩增 (PCR2) 步骤中通过 qPCR 进行定量。采用定量合并策略,根据估计的目标特异性唯一分子标识符 (UMI) 计数合并文库,以确保跨样本的每个目标序列 UMI 的读数一致。
elements_zh.main_results: 等深度池的测序证明了样本之间近乎均匀的每序列读取比率,从而以降低的成本确认了平衡的深度,而无需过采样。模拟显示,与等摩尔合并相比,等深度合并将所需测序读取的总数减少了约 70%,并且随着文库大小扩展,节省的金额也在增加。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将等深度池方法解释为一种稳健、可扩展且经济高效的批量 AIRRseq 研究策略,其中文库大小差异很大,消除了等摩尔池固有的复杂性相关的采样偏差。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这种方法可实现经济高效且标准化的 AIRRseq 分析,通过确保一致的测序深度和跨样本的可比较的 UMI 恢复率,可以增强登革热等传染病的免疫库研究。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 实施需要现有的校准数据集或试点测序实验来建立新工作流程或样本类型的 PCR2 Ct 值与相对 UMI 丰度之间的关系。由于依赖建模和模拟数据,证据强度中等。

title: Interactions Between Inbreeding, Fitness and the Bacterial Microbiome in Aedes aegypti Mosquitoes.
abstract: ABSTRACT Laboratory and field populations of insects can experience a decline in fitness and loss of genetic diversity due to inbreeding depression and genetic drift, respectively. Matings among related individuals and small population size may also influence insect host microbiomes with consequences for fitness. In the dengue vector mosquito, Aedes aegypti , the bacterial microbiome is largely environmentally determined, but recent studies have also revealed host genetic components. We generated a panel of 55 inbred lines from either of two founding outbred populations of Ae. aegypti to test for associations between life history traits, inbreeding, allelic diversity, and microbiome composition using ddRADseq and bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequencing on pools of mosquitoes. Effects of inbreeding were diverse, with severe composite fitness costs in many lines but minimal costs in others despite similar low levels of genetic diversity. We found no strong relationship between major life history traits across inbred lines, suggesting that any costs due to inbreeding were trait specific. Bacterial microbiome analysis of pooled samples from a subset of lines revealed common microbes across lines, with Elizabethkingia , Aeromonas , and Ralstonia being the most abundant. Despite bacterial composition varying widely, there was no clear relationship between microbiome composition and fitness or population origin. However, there were several significant positive correlations between the relative abundance of different microbial taxa across lines. Our results demonstrate diverse impacts of inbreeding on the fitness of mosquito populations but with limited impacts on the microbiome.

abstract_zh: 摘要 实验室和野外昆虫种群可能分别由于近交衰退和遗传漂变而经历适应性下降和遗传多样性丧失。相关个体之间的交配和小种群规模也可能影响昆虫 宿主 微生物组,从而对健康产生影响。在登革热 媒介 蚊子(埃及伊蚊)中,细菌微生物组很大程度上是由环境决定的,但最近的研究也揭示了 宿主 的遗传成分。我们从伊蚊的两个创始远交种群中生成了一组 55 个近交系。埃及伊蚊使用 ddRADseq 和细菌 16S rRNA 基因测序对蚊子池测试生活史特征、近交、等位基因多样性和微生物组组成之间的关联。近亲繁殖的影响是多种多样的,尽管遗传多样性水平相似,但许多品系的综合适应度成本很高,但其他品系的成本却很小。我们发现近交系的主要生活史性状之间没有很强的关系,这表明近交造成的任何成本都是性状特异性的。对来自部分品系子集的汇集样本进行的细菌微生物组分析揭示了跨品系的常见微生物,其中伊丽莎白金氏菌属、气单胞菌属和罗尔斯通氏菌属最丰富。尽管细菌组成差异很大,但微生物组组成与适应性或种群起源之间没有明确的关系。然而,不同品系微生物类群的相对丰度之间存在一些显着的正相关性。我们的结果表明,近亲繁殖对蚊子种群的适应性有多种影响,但对微生物组的影响有限。

title: Coincidence analysis: Identifying factors contributing to frontline health workers' confidence to face future pandemics across Honduras, Syria, and South Sudan.
abstract: Frontline health workers in humanitarian settings play a critical role in pandemic response, yet evidence on what sustains response readiness beyond the emergency is limited. This study examined factors associated with primary healthcare workers' sustained self-reported knowledge, skills, and confidence to respond to future outbreaks or pandemics, with the configurational analysis focused on confidence. A retrospective cross-sectional survey was conducted among 118 health workers in Honduras, Syria, and South Sudan who received COVID-19 training. Coincidence analysis was applied with a set of associated predictors to identify combinations of conditions linked to high sustained confidence. COVID-19 training that covered five or more core topics was associated with high sustained self-rated capacities; topics included proper use of personal protective equipment, transmission routes, procedures for case screening, and facility infection prevention and control. Continuity of primary healthcare services after emergency funding ended, fewer disruptions from conflict or natural disasters, and supportive team structures were linked to confidence. Coincidence analysis indicated multiple sufficient causal pathways to sustained confidence, the first being very high self-rated post-training knowledge as a standalone pathway (consistency: 0.66, coverage: 0.62). Other pathways included health workers with higher education combined with either case-screening training or working in facilities that continued services post-funding (consistency: 0.604, coverage: 0.64). Applying COVID-19 practices to other outbreaks (e.g., dengue, cholera) further reinforced capacities and illustrated the pathogen-agnostic value of core infection prevention and response competencies. Results underscore that durable preparedness at the primary healthcare level in fragile contexts depends on comprehensive, practice-oriented training for all types of frontline health workers, as well as enabling conditions that maintain service delivery. This study contributes to emerging literature using implementation science frameworks and coincidence analysis to understand complex causal pathways. The findings should inform global health security investments, including in the world's most fragile health systems.

title: Floods, Fevers, and Failed Systems: Building Climate-Resilient Public Health in Pakistan
abstract: Pakistan is once again facing a familiar crisis now a days. Since the beginning of the monsoon season in Pakistan on 26 June, 47 people have been reported killed and 123 injured in different provinces due to floods or flash floods. Flash floods have continued along major rivers in Punjab. This comes at a time when the country is still recovering from the 2025 floods that claimed the lives and livelihoods of more than 1037 people and displaced people to the tune of approximately 2.9 million during the period of peak flood [1, 2]. It is no longer an exception, but rather a trend, and in 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026 significant health emergency conditions were reported due to the flooding events [3]. In each cycle the same direction is taken. Sanitation facilities are washed away and drinking water sources are contaminated by flood water, families are displaced to relief areas, and stagnant water breeds disease vectors [1, 4]. In 2025, floods occurred in Punjab and resulted in more than 3500 reported Dengue cases, which was very high as compared to 2024 and thus a Province-wide Dengue Alert was issued [1]. In the relief camps of flood affected people in all over Punjab, the exposed population continued to be subjected to contaminated water and mosquitoes, which could lead to diarrhea, typhoid, malaria and dengue [2]. The downside of this trend is that it's very costly in terms of unnecessary morbidity. The same fragmented data reporting system could have undercounted similar outbreaks in the subsequent floods in 2022, as researchers have warned [2] and similar cholera and dengue data was recorded in 2022 for the flood alone in Sindh [5]. In addition to floods, Pakistan is experiencing a public health emergency over and over again, but without any reference to the basic needs of the people. There is further confirmation for this diagnosis given by recent analysis of the 2022 and 2025 floods. Drawing on the disaster management cycle, Akhter et al. found that the existing meteorological, hydrological and disease surveillance data systems were not linked, and that there were gaps in the data information systems, which led to failing forecasting and the lack of timely dissemination of early warning information, leaving high-risk districts unprepared for each flooding season [6]. The findings of these analyses point to the fact that the severity of flooding events does not seem to be the reason for the increasing number of public health crises in the country, but rather the failure to develop institutional capacity following previous public health crises. It will require an entirely new strategy to end this vicious cycle. Pakistan's health system has been treating the floods as a stand-alone event and has been reacting to outbreaks with spraying of larvicides after the event for the last two years. The missing component is climate-integrated public health infrastructure, including the pre-positioning of vector control and water-testing infrastructure and training of the workforce to view the initial response to flooding and the outbreak response as two sides of the same coin.

title: Zika virus positivity in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and its genomic landscape from Pune, Western India
abstract: Background and objectives Zika virus cases were confirmed from Pune, Western India, during an outbreak in June 2024. We conducted an entomological investigation in the Pune municipal corporation area and aimed to characterise the Zika virus from Aedes aegypti mosquitoes at the genomic level. Methods An entomological survey was conducted covering 16 locations in the Pune Municipal Corporation, between June and August 2024. Adult mosquitoes were collected using aspirators, while larvae were collected with the standard dipping and pipetting method. Aedes vector density was assessed, and samples were pooled. Zika virus positivity was assessed using real-time RT-qPCR. Genomic characterisation of the strains was achieved by whole-genome sequencing using the Oxford Nanopore technology platform. Results A high density of Aedes mosquitoes was revealed in the Pune area. Zika virus positivity was observed in 34/128 (26.5%) of Aedes aegypti mosquito pools. Full genome sequences of two ZIKV isolates were recovered from adult mosquito pools. Their time-scaled phylogenetic analysis showed grouping within the Asian lineage, having a recent ancestral time of evolution around 2014, indicating the introduction of newer virus strains in the recent past in India. Mutations E-V473M and motif E-VNDT, indicative of faster viral replication and higher mosquito infectivity, were noted in only one of the two isolates. Interpretation and conclusions With a high positivity of the Zika virus in Aedes aegypti , this study highlights the ongoing risk prevailing in the Pune municipal corporation area. Distinct characteristics of the circulating strains of the virus, and their evolutionary links to different global strains, underlines the importance of continuous genomic surveillance in vectors and hosts.

Their time-scaled phylogenetic analysis showed grouping within the Asian lineage, having a recent ancestral time of evolution around 2014, indicating the introduction of newer virus strains in the recent past in India. Mutations E-V473M and motif E-VNDT, indicative of faster viral replication and higher mosquito infectivity, were noted in only one of the two isolates. title: Paper-Based Biosensors for Monitoring Binding, Blocking, and Surrogate Neutralizing Antibody Responses Against Viral Infections
abstract: Virus-specific antibody responses, including binding antibodies and neutralizing antibodies (nAbs), are important indicators of antiviral immune status after infection or immunization. They provide complementary information on antiviral humoral immunity after infection or vaccination. Antigen-binding antibodies indicate previous exposure and the magnitude of the immune response, whereas receptor-blocking and functional neutralization assays assess whether antibodies interfere with viral entry or infection. Conventional neutralization assays, such as plaque reduction neutralization tests and pseudovirus neutralization tests, provide functional information but are labor-intensive, time-consuming, biosafety-restricted, and difficult to deploy for large-scale or decentralized monitoring. Paper-based biosensors, including lateral flow assays (LFAs), microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs), and paper-based ELISA, have emerged as promising point-of-care tools owing to their low cost, portability, simple operation, and compatibility with visual or digital readouts. This review critically evaluates these platforms according to whether they measure antigen-binding antibodies, receptor-blocking activity, surrogate neutralization, or functional neutralization and summarizes the applications of these three platforms for monitoring antibody responses against SARS-CoV-2, influenza, dengue, Zika, and monkeypox viruses. Unlike previous reviews that mainly focus on general paper-based biosensor design or conventional nAb assays, this review emphasizes the distinction between antigen-binding, receptor-blocking, and surrogate neutralization readouts, and critically discusses how paper-based signals should be interpreted in relation to functional immunity. We further analyze key translational challenges, including quantitative accuracy, antigen cross-reactivity, standardization, clinical validation, regulatory positioning, and real-world implementation. Future development should combine multiplex detection, standardized calibration, digital and AI-assisted interpretation, and clinically validated assay formats. Paper-based biosensors have considerable potential for decentralized antibody monitoring and public health surveillance, but their clinical utility depends on clear assay positioning and validation against appropriate functional or reference methods.

title: Evaluating Elevated D-Dimer Levels Associated Clinical Conditions in Hospitalised Patients: A Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Introduction: D-dimer is widely used to exclude Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) and to support the diagnosis of Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC). However, Elevated plasma D-dimer levels are not specific to thromboembolic disorders and may be observed in several non-thrombotic conditions such as infections, malignancies, inflammatory disorders, trauma, and postoperative states. This broad range of associated conditions complicates the interpretation of D-dimer results, particularly in resource-limited rural settings where the burden of infectious and inflammatory diseases is relatively high. Aim: To study the clinical conditions associated with elevated plasma D-dimer levels in hospitalised patients. Materials and Methods: The present cross-sectional, retrospective, laboratory database-based study was conducted in the Department of Pathology at a rural tertiary-care medical college in Western Maharashtra, India, from 1st October 2023 to 30th September 2024. Patients were selected from the Laboratory Information System (LIS) database based on records of quantitative plasma D-dimer testing performed during the study period. All consecutive hospitalised patients with at least one D-dimer value greater than 250 μg/L D-dimer Units (DDU), which represents the upper reference limit in the study laboratory, were included in the study. Demographic details, final clinical diagnosis, and selected laboratory parameters including Haemoglobin (Hb), Total Leukocyte Count (TLC), platelet count, Prothrombin Time/International Normalised Ratio (PT/INR), Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT), C-Reactive Protein (CRP), and other available laboratory investigations were retrieved from hospital records. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics. Results: Among 349 D-dimer tests, 247 were >250 μg/L DDU. After excluding duplicate tests (n=6) and cases with insufficient clinical information (n=6), 235 patients were analysed (139 males, 59.1%; 96 females, 40.9%). D-dimer values ranged from 255 to 75,860 μg/L DDU (mean 2,604.3 μg/L). The commonest cause was dengue (133/235, 56.6%), comprising 129 NS1 antigen-positive and 4 IgM-positive cases. Cardiovascular disorders {Myocardial infarction, Atrial Fibrillation, post Coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG)} constituted 28/235 (11.9%), followed by sepsis (16/235, 6.8%) and thromboembolic conditions (12/235, 5.1%). Other causes included Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS), fracture/osteomyelitis, pregnancy-related conditions, malignancy, snakebite and acute febrile illness. Overall mortality was 35/235 (14.9%) and was predominantly seen in patients with moderate-to-severe D-dimer elevation. Conclusion: In the current rural hospital cohort, elevated D-dimer levels were most frequently associated with infectious conditions particularly dengue followed by cardiovascular disorders and sepsis, whereas confirmed thromboembolic events represented a small proportion of cases. Extremely high values were observed in severe systemic illnesses such as sepsis and snakebite and were associated with poorer outcomes. These findings suggest that, in tropical rural settings, elevated D-dimer often reflects infection-related coagulation activation rather than isolated thromboembolism. Clinical interpretation should therefore be guided by the underlying disease context.

title: Situational health diagnosis in the rural parish of Noboa, Ecuador: a descriptive cross-sectional study on the mixed burden of disease and access barriers
abstract: This study aimed to comprehensively characterize the health situation of Noboa parish, Manabí, Ecuador, during 2024. An observational, descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted with 90 inhabitants selected through non-probabilistic convenience sampling, using a structured questionnaire and reviewing local health facility records. Descriptive statistics were applied for analysis. A total of 28 communicable disease cases were identified, with coronavirus (34.5%) and dengue (27.6%) predominating; among non-communicable chronic conditions (11 cases), arterial hypertension (27.3%) and diabetes mellitus (18.2%) were most frequent. Over half of the population (55.6%) lacked access to prevention programs, while alcohol consumption (38.9%) and a history of tobacco use (33.3%) were reported. Problem prioritization ranked acute respiratory infections in children and geographical access barriers as leading health issues. Noboa parish faces a mixed burden of communicable and chronic diseases, compounded by behavioral risk factors and limited preventive access, underscoring the need to strengthen primary care through health education, epidemiological surveillance, and expanded preventive coverage.

title: Potential Mechanisms Underlying Bleeding During Infection With Hemorrhagic Fever Viruses.
abstract: Viral hemorrhagic fever (VHF) describes different diseases caused by several viruses from 6 virus families: Filoviridae , Nairoviridae , Phenuiviridae , Hepadnaviridae , Arenaviridae , and Flaviviridae . VHF was once considered a geographically localized problem, but, due to expanding vector ranges and increased human contact with animal reservoirs and hosts, the number of VHF cases is increasing. As the name indicates, VHF is associated with bleeding. Both direct effects from viral infection of host cells and indirect effects caused by the host response to the virus contribute to the dysregulation of the hemostatic system. Many studies have measured different parameters and various biomarkers in samples from infected humans and nonhuman primate models. For example, Ebola virus infection in a nonhuman primate model leads to increased TF (tissue factor) expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and extracellular vesicles. In dengue virus infection, thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction occur. There are likely both common and distinct mechanisms underlying bleeding in different VHFs, as sites of bleeding differ between the viruses. Herein, we discuss the potential mechanisms leading to bleeding during VHF, which include a consumptive coagulopathy, decreased coagulation factor production, thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction, and endothelial cell activation and damage, resulting in increased vascular permeability. While a significant body of work exists examining different aspects of the various viral infections that may lead to bleeding, there are still many open questions and areas for investigation. Therefore, more studies are needed to better understand the mechanisms underlying bleeding in VHF caused by different viruses.

title: Smart Waste Solutions for Disaster Prevention – Building Urban Resilience in Gaya
abstract: Rapid urbanization and population growth have intensified solid waste management (SWM) challenges in Gaya, the second largest city of Bihar, India. Inefficient collection, open dumping, uncontrolled burning, and inadequate disposal practices have not only degraded the urban environment but also heightened disaster risks, particularly through public health hazards, urban flooding, and water pollution. Clogged drains during monsoon seasons and indiscriminate waste disposal on roadsides and vacant lands exacerbate urban flooding, while untreated wastewater directly discharged into the Falgu River contributes to severe environmental contamination and the spread of vector-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, and diarrheal infections. This study investigates the intersections between urban growth, slum population dynamics, waste generation trends, and existing SWM practices in Gaya. It emphasizes the city’s heightened vulnerability to disaster risks stemming from poor waste governance. The analysis highlights the urgent need for integrated strategies including systematic waste segregation at source, enhanced recycling, adoption of sanitary landfills, and active community participation in household waste management. Findings suggest that sustainable SWM practices can significantly mitigate disaster risks by reducing health hazards, preventing urban flooding, and improving resilience of critical urban infrastructure. For Gaya, adopting such practices holds transformative potential—not only for protecting public health and urban populations but also for safeguarding its cultural heritage and ensuring a safe, resilient, and sustainable urban future.

title: Colonisation and temperature-driven variation in life-history traits of the West Nile virus vector Culex pipiens at its Northern European limit
abstract: Abstract Background Mosquito-borne diseases (MBDs) are increasing worldwide driven by factors such as travel, land-use change, global trade, and climate warming. In Europe, Culex pipiens sensu lato (s.l.)—the primary vector of West Nile and Usutu viruses—is widespread and an increasing public-health concern with recent detection of WNV in English mosquitoes and ongoing climate change underscoring risks in northern regions. However, data on how temperature affects life-history traits of high-latitude populations remain limited, hindering accurate predictions of vectorial capacity. Methods We used field-collected larvae in Scotland to establish a colony of Culex pipiens and performed its molecular characterisation by PCR, including Wolbachia presence. We then assessed the effects of temperature on key life-history traits, including development time, adult longevity, and body size. Results We successfully established a colony of Culex pipiens pipiens infected with Wolbachia at its northern range limit. We observed that temperature increase speeds up the embryonic, larval and pupal development while reducing the adult longevity and adult size. Interestingly, this northern colony display the longest adult survival ever described for non blood fed Cx. pipiens at all temperature examined. Conclusions Our findings provide critical baseline data for this northern population and offer methodological guidance for establishing Cx. pipiens colonies from field material. These results improve our understanding of thermal sensitivity in Northern Culex mosquitoes and will support future modelling of population dynamics and MBD risk under climate change.

full_text: Abstract Background The increasing incidence of dengue in Europe, combined with the spread of invasive mosquito species, raises concerns about the emergence of new vectors. Aedes koreicus, an invasive mosquito rapidly expanding in several European countries, has shown competence for some arboviruses, but its role in dengue virus transmission remains unknown. This study aimed to assess, for the first time, the vector competence of an Italian population of Ae. koreicus for dengue virus serotype 1 (DENV-1). Methods Laboratory-reared Ae. koreicus females originating from northeastern Italy were orally infected with DENV-1 via an artificial blood meal. Mosquitoes were maintained at 26 ± 1 °C and analysed at 7, 14, 21 and 28 days post-infection (dpi). Infection, dissemination and transmission were evaluated by RT-qPCR and droplet digital PCR, while the presence of infectious virus in saliva was confirmed by virus isolation in Vero E6 cells. Results Aedes koreicus was susceptible to DENV-1 infection, with infection rates ranging from 30 to 60% across time points. Viral dissemination to legs and wings was detected from 14 dpi onwards, reaching 100% at 21 and 28 dpi. DENV-1 RNA was detected in saliva at 28 days post-infection (dpi), indicating a relatively long extrinsic incubation period. Overall transmission rate and efficiency were 33.3% and 20%, respectively, at later time points. Infectious virus was successfully isolated from saliva samples confirming transmission capability. Conclusions Aedes koreicus was shown to be susceptible to DENV-1 infection and capable of transmitting the virus, although with low efficiency and a long extrinsic incubation period. Despite these limitations, its increasing abundance, longevity and capacity to feed on humans suggest that it may act as a potential dengue vector under favourable conditions. These findings highlight the need to include Ae. koreicus in entomological surveillance and risk assessments for dengue transmission in Europe. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the vector competence of Aedes koreicus, an invasive mosquito species in Italy, for dengue virus serotype 1 (DENV-1). Laboratory-reared mosquitoes were orally infected with DENV-1 and analyzed at multiple time points. Results showed that Ae. koreicus was susceptible to DENV-1 infection with infection rates ranging from 30 to 60%, and viral dissemination reached 100% by 21 days post-infection. DENV-1 RNA was detected in saliva at 28 days, confirming transmission capability, though with low efficiency (20%) and a long extrinsic incubation period. The findings suggest that Ae. koreicus could potentially act as a dengue vector under favorable conditions, highlighting the need for its inclusion in European entomological surveillance and risk assessments.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 欧洲登革热 发病率 的增加,加上入侵蚊种的传播,引起了人们对新 媒介 出现的担忧。本研究旨在首次评估意大利伊蚊群体的 媒介 能力。koreicus 为 登革病毒 血清型 1 (DENV-1)。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 实验室培养的 Ae。来自意大利东北部的雌性 koreicus 通过人工血粉经口感染 DENV-1。将蚊子维持在 26 ± 1 °C,并在感染后 7、14、21 和 28 天 (dpi) 进行分析。
elements_zh.methods: 通过 RT-qPCR 和液滴数字 PCR 评估感染、传播和 传播,同时通过 Vero E6 细胞中的病毒分离证实唾液中感染性病毒的存在。
elements_zh.main_results: Aedes koreicus was susceptible to DENV-1 infection, with infection rates ranging from 30 to 60% across time points. Viral dissemination to legs and wings was detected from 14 dpi onwards, reaching 100% at 21 and 28 dpi. DENV-1 RNA was detected in saliva at 28 days post-infection (dpi), indicating a relatively long extrinsic incubation period.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 朝鲜伊蚊被证明对 DENV-1 感染敏感,并且能够传播病毒,但效率低且外源性潜伏期长。尽管存在这些限制,但其不断增加的丰度、寿命和以人类为食的能力表明,在有利的条件下,它可能充当潜在的登革热 媒介。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了将 Ae 纳入其中的必要性。koreicus 在欧洲昆虫学 监测 和登革热 传播 风险评估中的应用。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于该研究基于实验室的性质以及观察到的 传播 效率相对较低,因此证据强度中等。该研究是在受控条件下进行的,可能无法完全反映现实世界的 传播 动态。

full_text: Abstract Purpose of Review Vector-borne diseases (VBDs) represent 17% of the global infectious disease burden, expanding rapidly due to an interconnected matrix of climate change, rapid urbanization, land-use modifications, and globalization. This review analyzes advancements in controlling pathogens such as dengue, malaria, Chagas disease, leishmaniasis, and Oropouche virus. Recent Findings Findings highlight a transition toward precision biotechnology: the use of Wolbachia and gene editing; dual-action nets and new vaccines; and the “One Health” approach. The emergence of viruses like Oropouche and the necessity of monitoring unconventional vectors are emphasized. Effective control in the Anthropocene requires moving beyond single-strategy solutions, integrating artificial intelligence, digital surveillance, and interventions at the human-animal-environment interface. Summary Success depends on addressing socio-climatic determinants and fostering the resilience of adaptive health systems. full_text: Abstract Mosquito-borne diseases are a major public health concern. This study investigated mosquito species richness, relative abundance, and seasonal dynamics in District Bajaur, Pakistan. To assess the seasonal diversity and abundance of mosquitoes in District Bajaur and their potential role in malaria and dengue fever transmission. Adult and larval mosquitoes were sampled through standard collection methods, from multiple locations including cattle sheds, human dwellings, bathrooms, and animal bait. sampling was carried out from October 2023 to September 2024 according to WHO protocol. A total of 33,173 adult and 6303 larval mosquitoes, comprising five genera and 16 species were collected. Culex was the most dominant genus (63%), primarily Cx. quinquefasciatus (37%) and Cx. pipiens (25%). Aedes accounted for 20%, led by Ae. albopictus (13%) and Ae. aegypti (6%), while Anopheles comprised 16%, dominated by An. culicifacies (12%). Armigeres and Mansonia were rare. Indoor collections (26,580 mosquitoes) revealed higher abundance in cattle sheds, followed by human dwellings and bathrooms. Seasonal variation was evident, with peaks in July to August and minimal activity in winter. Cx. quinquefasciatus, Cx. pipiens, Ae. albopictus, and An. culicifacies were the most persistent species, present year-round and demonstrating ecological adaptability. Larval assessment confirmed strong seasonality, with peak abundance in August and no larvae detected in January. Statistical analyses revealed significant differences in the distributions across most species, though not in immature stages. Enhanced entomological surveillance during and after monsoon seasons is crucial for effectively controlling dengue, malaria, and similar mosquito-borne diseases. Data availability Supporting data for the findings presented in this study, such as mosquito collection records, species abundance, and seasonal distribution data from Bajaur, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, have been presented within the manuscript and supplementary information files. Raw data can also be obtained from the corresponding author on reasonable request. full_text_excerpt: This study investigated mosquito species richness, relative abundance, and seasonal dynamics in District Bajaur, Pakistan. Adult and larval mosquitoes were sampled through standard collection methods, from multiple locations including cattle sheds, human dwellings, bathrooms, and animal bait. Data availability Supporting data for the findings presented in this study, such as mosquito collection records, species abundance, and seasonal distribution data from Bajaur, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, have been presented within the manuscript and supplementary information files. To assess the seasonal diversity and abundance of mosquitoes in District Bajaur and their potential role in malaria and dengue fever transmission. sampling was carried out from October 2023 to September 2024 according to WHO protocol. A total of 33,173 adult and 6303 larval mosquitoes, comprising five genera and 16 species were collected. Culex was the most dominant genus (63%), primarily Cx. quinquefasciatus (37%) and Cx. Aedes accounted for 20%, led by Ae. albopictus (13%) and Ae. aegypti (6%), while Anopheles comprised 16%, dominated by An. Armigeres and Mansonia were rare. Indoor collections (26,580 mosquitoes) revealed higher abundance in cattle sheds, followed by human dwellings and bathrooms. Seasonal variation was evident, with peaks in July to August and minimal activity in winter. quinquefasciatus, Cx. culicifacies were the most persistent species, present year-round and demonstrating ecological adaptability.
